title: Channel-length modulation and output resistance ro

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
An ideal saturated MOSFET is a perfect current source, but real output curves slope upward. As \(V_{DS}\) rises, the depletion region at the drain widens and the pinch-off point moves toward the source. The effective channel length \(L - \Delta L\) shrinks and the current rises. This is **channel-length modulation** (CLM), modelled by a factor \((1 + \lambda V_{DS})\).

The slope of the output curve defines the **output resistance** \(r_o\), the small-signal resistance between drain and source. Extending the saturated lines backward, they all meet the axis at \(V_{DS} = -1/\lambda\), the MOS counterpart of the BJT's Early voltage. Because \(\Delta L\) is roughly fixed, \(\lambda\) scales as \(1/L\): longer channels give higher \(r_o\). The product \(g_mr_o\), the **intrinsic gain**, is the most voltage gain one transistor can provide, and it depends only on \(\lambda\) and \(V_{ov}\).

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ I_D = \tfrac12\mu_nC_{ox}\tfrac WLV_{ov}^2(1 + \lambda V_{DS}) \]
\[ r_o = \left(\frac{\partial I_D}{\partial V_{DS}}\right)^{-1} \approx \frac1{\lambda I_D}, \qquad g_mr_o = \frac2{\lambda V_{ov}} \]
sections.figure_alt: NMOS output curves with channel-length modulation: after the knee at V_DS = V_ov each curve keeps rising slowly with V_DS instead of staying flat.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: A device with \(\lambda = 0.04\ \mathrm{V^{-1}}\) at \(I_D = 0.25\ \mathrm{mA}\) has \(r_o = 1/(0.04\cdot0.25\ \mathrm{mA}) = 100\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\). At \(V_{ov} = 0.2\ \mathrm{V}\) its intrinsic gain is \(2/(0.04\cdot0.2) = 250\). Doubling \(L\) at the same current and overdrive would roughly double both.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Placing the extrapolated intercept at \(+1/\lambda\) instead of \(-1/\lambda\).
- Treating \(r_o\) as fixed; it scales as \(1/I_D\).
- Using the triode slope near the knee to estimate \(\lambda\); only saturated points apply.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: \(r_o\) completes the small-signal model and limits every high-gain stage. It sets the output resistance of current mirrors, and cascodes exist to multiply it.
